subject: A survey plan of the reed's cycle: one surveyed ring round the wind chest, with reeds a and b as two stations on it whose angle apart is the beat.
controls: press: the ring's radius grows from 52 to 92 px (and with it the stations' distance from the chest); scale.
reed: the chainage ticks round the ring go from 12 to 36; count.
leak: the ring breaks into a dashed run on its lower side, 0 to 10 gaps, with short bearing lines escaping through them; count.

choir: station b leaves station a and travels round the ring, 0 to 150 degrees apart; rotation. While a note is held the two stations orbit at their two rates, so the gap opens and closes at the beat rate.
risks: Stretch, and only half earns it. The exception: choir is two reeds a few cents apart, and two bodies on one orbit at slightly different rates is literally what beating is, so the orbit is true for choir and, held, shows the beat at the beat rate. It doesn't fit the rest: press as ring radius, reed as tick count and leak as gaps are scenery bolted to the orrery, the failure P13 warns about (Dens and Crpt fit, Scal and Kit didn't). There's no cycle of items here, just two. A plan is flat by definition, so craft.md's 'think in 3D' doesn't apply, but it also loses the orrery's depth. Constant orbital motion while notes are held is a big redraw cost only if the ring itself moves; it doesn't.
